title: BlockMargin - Interest Rate Futures on Cardano

ms.promise:
1. Price Oracle that publishes 3m SOFR Futures daily prices on the Cardano Preview Testnet
2. A Pricer as a backend service API that accepts trade characteristics as inputs and returns back the fair price for the instrument
2. A Risk Engine as a backend service API that accepts the price and trade characteristics as inputs and returns back an estimate of how much the price can move over the next 2 days 

Other considerations
For the Price Oracle:
We will build a daemon that reads their settlement prices once a day, after the market closes, and records them onto the Cardano Preview testnet. A proof of concept of this has been built and a trial ran where these prices were recorded as metadata back in 2021 using https://nut.link/ and https://github.com/functionally/mantis-oracle. We will investigate the possibility of using Marlowe oracles, which already comes with a SOFR rate as explained in this article: https://github.com/input-output-hk/marlowe-cardano/blob/main/marlowe-apps/Oracle.md#custom-external-feeds

ms.promise:
1. A smart contract factor will generate new smart contracts for each new transaction.
2. A front end user interface to initiate a trade and manage it through out its life that uses the smart contract factory - running on the Cardano Preview testnet

A web-based dashboard to which a user can connect and interact with the smart contract - the correctness of interaction is not judged in this milestone, only the ability to generate smart contracts for different instrument characteristics. Correctness is the subject of the next milestone
The dashboard will allow for connected users to create a new smart contract that will encode the characteristics of a SOFR future. The smart contract generator will perform this task and return back the smart contract CBORHex (or its equivalent in Marlowe) which the user will use to initiate the SOFR futures test transaction.
The dashboard in the form of a webpage URL will be open for the community to test, and we will provide a short video with the steps of how to use it on a Cardano testnet.

Notes:

ms.criteria:
1. The smart contract can be generated by a user from the front end user interface and a new trade initiated. This is done by connecting with a Cardano compatible web wallet to the front end.
2. The front end shows the initiated smart contract and the outstanding actions. Collateral can be posted and redeemed using the dashboard

ms.promise:
1. A test trade will be done on the testnet to validate functionality and identify bugs. It will be run over 7 days to check the initial trade and daily collateral management functionalities. At the end, the trade will be closed out and cashflows exchanged. Alternative scenarios of large market moves will be tested.
The test trade needs to be balanced between covering the possible range of market scenarios and possible user interactions and be done within a reasonable amount of time. The following battery of tests will be run, noting that these might change as we progress through development and amend the set of features and user interaction
- user 1st initiates the transaction and sets the wallet address of the 2nd user
- the 2nd user sees a new trade and its characteristics in their dashboard and accepts the trade
- after the trade is accepted, both users need to post initial margin for the trade to start
- both users posts margin (the contract should initiate correctly)
- only 1 user posts margin (the contract should not initiate)
- next day the market moves, both users see the change in the value of their position and the additional margin they need to post, or can withdraw
